speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your skin lesions, please describe their appearance, including size, color, shape, and any symptoms like itching or bleeding. Also, how long have you noticed them?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history; the combination of a non-healing, crusty lesion on the penile shaft and a similar one on your finger, along with your significant smoking history and failed treatments in your home country, is very concerning. Given the high suspicion for squamous cell carcinoma in these locations, have you noticed any changes in the size, color, or texture of these lesions, or any associated pain or discharge?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (Penile and Cutaneous). The presence of non-healing, crusty, painless lesions in a high-risk patient with a significant smoking history and failed treatments for syphilis and eczema is highly indicative of malignancy. While the clinical picture is strong, I am requesting histopathological confirmation via biopsy for both lesions to rule out other differentials definitively. REQUEST TEST: Biopsy_Penile_Lesion, Biopsy_Finger_Lesion.
